correctness.rationale: The integer half-shadow weights have counts (12,32,4) at weights (0,1,2), total 40; a sign-case proof shows each of the 384 source decks has weight at least 2. Hence every code has at most 20 words. The ten explicit tuples and their negations yield 20 distinct codewords with pairwise disjoint deletion sets. The actual standalone script checks forward deletions and independently generated inverse insertions on every source/recipient incidence; it verifies the 384 dual constraints and 46 distinct outputs. No optimizer termination or numerical estimate is used as proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A direct equivalence would need to preserve both sign tuples and the absolute-rank renormalization of every deletion. Therefore the cited results do not identify the forty-unit weighted certificate or a twenty-source disjoint signed-deck packing.

value.rationale: The problem is a natural first small benchmark for unknown deletion of one oriented rank, where the missing rank and sign are lost but relative order and surviving signs remain. Its exact 20-message capacity has a short transparent weight certificate and an explicitly sign-complement-closed optimum, demonstrating a genuinely nontrivial interaction between orientation and standardized ranks. It does not claim a paper-scale general capacity formula or arbitrary extensions.
